source.primary_witnesses: Aramaic DSS fragments (4Q201-4Q207; late 3rd c. BCE through 1st c. BCE) where preserved; Greek Akhmim Panopolitanus (6th c. CE) where Aramaic absent; Ge'ez (medieval; the only complete witness) as fallback
source.transliteration_convention: Scholarly conventions: Aramaic Imperial-Aramaic transliteration per Milik 1976 (ḥ ṣ ʿ ḫ); Greek SBL convention (η→ē, ω→ō, θ→th, etc., matching Matthew precedent); Ge'ez SBL Ge'ez convention (ḫ ḫ̣ ʾ ʿ ä for ä-vowel)
source.verificationStatus: best-effort reconstruction; verification pending against Milik 1976 DJD apparatus + Nickelsburg 2001 Hermeneia + original codicology
source.fetchedFrom: Milik 1976 The Books of Enoch + Black 1985 Greek text + Charles 1912 Ge'ez PD + Knibb 1978 Ge'ez critical edition + Nickelsburg 2001 Hermeneia commentary
source.citation: Milik 1976 The Books of Enoch (Oxford); Black 1985 The Book of Enoch or 1 Enoch (SVTP 7, Leiden); Nickelsburg 2001 1 Enoch 1 Hermeneia; Charles 1912 The Book of Enoch (Oxford, PD); Knibb 1978 The Ethiopic Book of Enoch (Oxford); Tigchelaar-García Martínez 2000 DJD XXXVI; VanderKam 1984 Enoch and the Growth of an Apocalyptic Tradition; Reed 2005 Fallen Angels.
source.paleography_note: The layered-witness convention reflects the manuscript-attestation reality: Aramaic DSS fragments are FRAGMENTARY (preserve only portions of chs 1-36); Greek Akhmim Panopolitanus preserves chs 1-32 substantially complete; Ge'ez is the only complete witness but the most distant in time and language from the Aramaic original. Per-verse selection prioritizes the oldest preserved witness; alternate witnesses documented where they differ materially or provide cross-collation value.

verses.text: והוה כדי שגיו בני אנשא בארעא והתילדו להון בנן בנת שפירן
verses.translit: wa-hăwāh kědī šāgīw běnē ʾănāšāʾ bě-ʾarʿāʾ wĕ-hitēlědū lěhōn bĕnān bĕnāt šappīrān
verses.text_greek: Καὶ ἐγένετο οὗ ἂν ἐπληθύνθησαν οἱ υἱοὶ τῶν ἀνθρώπων ἐν ἐκείναις ταῖς ἡμέραις, ἐγεννήθησαν αὐτοῖς θυγατέρες ὡραῖαι καὶ καλαί.
verses.text_geez: ወኮነ፡ ሶበ፡ በዝኁ፡ ውሉደ፡ ሰብእ፡ በውእቱ፡ መዋዕል፡ ተወልዳ፡ ሎሙ፡ አዋልድ፡ ሠናያት፡ ወላህያት፡
verses.notes: **MAJOR LENS-RISK + CROSS-CORPUS SITE — beginning of the Watchers myth.** Direct paraphrase of Gen 6:1: 'when men began to multiply on the face of the earth, and daughters were born to them.' The Aramaic phrasing closely matches the Hebrew of Gen 6:1 — the Watchers narrative is a sustained midrash on Gen 6:1-4. Cross-corpus: Gen 6:1-4 (the bnei elohim + Nephilim notice); Jub 5:1-2; CD 2:17-19 (Damascus Document Watchers reference).

verses.text: וחזו אנון עירין בני שמיא וחמדו אנון ואמרו דן לדן איתון נבחר לן נשין מן בנת אנשא ונולד לן בנין
verses.translit: wa-ḥăzō ʾinnōn ʿīrīn bĕnē šĕmayyāʾ wĕ-ḥămadū ʾinnōn wĕ-ʾamarū dēn lě-dēn ʾītōn niḇḥar lan něšīn min běnāt ʾănāšāʾ wĕ-nōlēd lan běnīn
verses.text_greek: καὶ ἐθεάσαντο αὐτὰς οἱ ἐγρήγοροι, υἱοὶ οὐρανοῦ, καὶ ἐπεθύμησαν αὐτάς, καὶ εἶπαν πρὸς ἀλλήλους· Δεῦτε ἐκλεξώμεθα ἑαυτοῖς γυναῖκας ἀπὸ τῶν ἀνθρώπων, καὶ γεννήσωμεν ἑαυτοῖς τέκνα.
verses.text_geez: ወርእዩ፡ መላእክት፡ ውሉደ፡ ሰማይ፡ ወፈተውዎን፡ ወተባሀሉ፡ በበይናቲሆሙ፡ ንዑ፡ ንምከር፡ ንርአይ፡ ለነ፡ አንስተ፡ እምውሉደ፡ ሰብእ፡ ወንለድ፡ ለነ፡ ውሉደ፡
verses.witness_primary: 4Q201 1 iii 3-5 + 4Q202 1 ii 2-3 (Milik 1976 pp. 150-152) — Aramaic preserved: KEY TERMS עירין 'Watchers' + בני שמיא 'sons of heaven'
verses.notes: **MAJOR LENS-RISK + CROSS-CORPUS SITE.** The Watchers (עירין / ἐγρήγοροι) see the daughters of men, lust after them, plan to take wives. Aramaic עירין בני שמיא 'Watchers, sons of heaven' explicitly identifies the Genesis 6 בני האלהים 'sons of God / sons of the gods' with the Watchers. The Ge'ez here departs slightly — using መላእክት 'angels' (an interpretive flattening) rather than 'Watchers.' Cross-corpus: Gen 6:2 (bnei elohim / huioi tou theou in LXX); cf. Job 1:6, 2:1, 38:7; Ps 29:1, 89:7. The lens-risk is the Watchers-as-extraterrestrials reading the canon engages — Editor will handle the framing.

verses.text: ואמר שמיחזה רבהון דחל אנה דלא תצבון למעבד עבדא דנא ואנה בלחודי אהוה חיב חטא רב
verses.translit: wa-ʾămar Šĕmīḥăzāh rabbhōn dāḥel ʾanāh dī-lāʾ tiṣbōn lě-meʿbad ʿăbādāʾ dĕnāʾ wa-ʾănāh bi-lḥōdī ʾehēweh ḥayyāḇ ḥăṭāʾ rab
verses.text_greek: καὶ εἶπεν Σεμιαζᾶς ὁ ἄρχων αὐτῶν πρὸς αὐτούς· Φοβοῦμαι μὴ οὐ θελήσετε ποιῆσαι τὸ πρᾶγμα τοῦτο, καὶ ἔσομαι ἐγὼ μόνος ὀφειλέτης ἁμαρτίας μεγάλης.
verses.text_geez: ወይቤ፡ ሰማይዓዛ፡ ዘውእቱ፡ መልአኮሙ፡ እፈርህ፡ ከመ፡ ኢትፈቅዱ፡ ግቢረ፡ ዘንተ፡ ግብረ፡ ወእከውን፡ አንሰ፡ ባሕቲትየ፡ በዓለ፡ ኃጢአት፡ ዐባይ፡
verses.witness_primary: 4Q201 1 iii 6-9 + 4Q202 1 ii 4-6 (Milik 1976 pp. 150-155) — KEY PRESERVATION of Šemiḥazah's name in Aramaic original
verses.notes: **Šemiḥazah (Aramaic ŠMYḤZH) — the Watchers' chief — named.** The name etymologically reads as šēm-ḥăzāh 'the Name has seen' or šĕmī-ḥăzāh 'my Name has seen' (Milik 1976 pp. 152-153; Nickelsburg 2001 pp. 179-180). Greek Σεμιαζᾶς (Semiazas), Ge'ez ሰማይዓዛ (Sĕmayʿāzā) — both reflect the Aramaic. The character argues that he alone should not bear the responsibility — the chiefs' oath in v. 4-5 results. Cross-corpus: cf. Asael as the parallel chief in 1 En 8-10 (the bifurcation Šemiḥazah-leader vs. Asael-knowledge-revealer is one of the textual cruxes of 1 En 6-11).

verses.text: וענו כלהון ואמרו לה נומה כלן וניחרים אנחנא כלן בחרמא דלא נשבק עצא דא ועד דנעבד עבדא דן
verses.translit: wa-ʿănō kullhōn wa-ʾămarū leh nōmāh kullan wĕ-niḥrim ʾănaḥnāʾ kullan bě-ḥermāʾ dī-lāʾ nišbōq ʿēṣāʾ dāʾ wĕ-ʿad dī-naʿbed ʿăbādāʾ dēn
verses.text_greek: καὶ ἀπεκρίθησαν αὐτῷ πάντες καὶ εἶπαν· Ὀμόσωμεν ὅρκῳ πάντες, καὶ ἀναθεματίσωμεν πάντες ἀλλήλους, μὴ ἀποστρέψαι τὴν γνώμην ταύτην, μέχρις ἂν τελέσωμεν αὐτὴν καὶ ποιήσωμεν τὸ πρᾶγμα τοῦτο.
verses.text_geez: ወአውሥእዎ፡ ኵሎሙ፡ ወይቤልዎ፡ ነማሐል፡ ኵልነ፡ ወንተሐራረም፡ ኵልነ፡ በበይናቲነ፡ ከመ፡ ኢንሚጥ፡ ምክረነ፡ ዘንተ፡ እስከ፡ አመ፡ ንፌጽም፡ ግብረ፡ ዘንተ፡
verses.notes: The Watchers' mutual oath. The term ḥerem (חרמא, ban / anathema) is the technical Aramaic for the binding oath. The Greek ἀναθεματίσωμεν parallels. Cross-corpus: cf. CD 16:7-9 (oath legislation in Damascus Document).

verses.text: באדין כלהון אומיו כחדא וחרמו כלהון על כן
verses.translit: bě-ʾēdayin kullhōn ʾōmīw kě-ḥădāʾ wĕ-ḥerimū kullhōn ʿal kēn
verses.text_greek: Τότε πάντες ὁμοῦ ὤμοσαν καὶ ἀνεθεμάτισαν πάντες ἀλλήλους ἐν αὐτοῖς.
verses.text_geez: ወይእተ፡ አሚረ፡ ኵሎሙ፡ ሕቡረ፡ መሐሉ፡ ወተሐራረሙ፡ በበይናቲሆሙ፡
verses.notes: The oath formally sworn — execution of v. 4.

verses.text: והוו כלהון מאתין די נחתו ביומי ירד לראש טור חרמון
verses.translit: wa-hăwō kullhōn mě-ʾātīn dī něḥătū bě-yōmē Yāred lě-rēʾš ṭūr Ḥermōn
verses.text_greek: καὶ ἦσαν οἱ πάντες διακόσιοι· καὶ κατέβησαν ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις Ἰάρεδ εἰς τὴν κορυφὴν τοῦ Ἑρμωνιεὶμ ὄρους.
verses.text_geez: ወኮኑ፡ ኵሎሙ፡ ምእትኒሆሙ፡ ወወረዱ፡ በመዋዕለ፡ ያሬድ፡ ውስተ፡ ርእሰ፡ ደብረ፡ አርሞን፡
verses.witness_primary: 4Q201 1 iii 13-14 + 4Q202 1 ii 9-10 (Milik 1976 pp. 150-156) — CRITICAL: 'Mount Hermon' preserved in Aramaic original
verses.notes: **MAJOR LENS-RISK SITE — MT HERMON DESCENT.** The 200 Watchers descend on Mount Hermon during the days of Jared (Enoch's father — Gen 5:18-19). **The etymological wordplay**: ירד (Yared) means 'descent / he came down,' and the Watchers' descent (נחתו) occurs in his days — Hermon (חרמון) cognate with ḥerem 'oath/ban' — the mountain of the oath. This wordplay is preserved in the Aramaic and is one of the indicators of Aramaic-original composition (the wordplay does not work as cleanly in Greek or Ge'ez). The Greek Ἑρμωνιεὶμ is a Greek transliteration of Aramaic חרמון. Cross-corpus: Mount Hermon is the northern cosmic-mountain in the OT (Ps 89:13, 133:3); cf. Cana mythology of Baal on Mt Saphon/Hermon. The Hermon descent is one of the canon's central topographical interests (canon: 'where did the Elohim descend?' — site of major engagement).

verses.text: ואלין שמהת רביהון שמיחזה הוא רבהון ארעתקפ תניהון רמאל תליתיהון כוכבאל רביעיהון ברקאל חמישיהון זקיאל שתיתיהון ארטקיפא שביעיהון חננאל תמיניהון תורי תשיעיהון שמשיאל עשיריהון שהריאל חד עשיר תוריאל תרי עשיר ימיאל תלת עשיר יומיאל ארבעת עשיר סהריאל חמשת עשיר אסאל שתת עשיר רעמיאל שבעת עשיר עזזאל תמנת עשיר משריאל תשעת עשיר רובאל עשרא עזיאל
verses.translit: wĕ-ʾillēn šĕmāhāt rabbēhōn: Šĕmīḥăzāh hūʾ rabbhōn, ʾArʿătqōp, Rāmʾēl, Kōkabʾēl, Bărāqʾēl, Zīqīʾēl, ʾArtĕqīpāʾ, Ḥănānʾēl, Tūrīʾēl, Šamšīʾēl, Šaḥrīʾēl, Tūrʾēl, Yōmʾēl, Yōmīʾēl, Sahrīʾēl, ʾAsʾēl, Raʿamʾēl, ʿAzazʾēl, Mašrīʾēl, Rūbʾēl, ʿAzīʾēl
verses.text_greek: καὶ ταῦτα τὰ ὀνόματα τῶν ἀρχόντων αὐτῶν· Σεμιαζᾶς ὁ ἄρχων αὐτῶν, Ἀταρκουφ, Ἀραθακ, Χωβαβιήλ, Ὠραμμαμή, Ῥαμιήλ, Σαμψίχ, Ζακιήλ, Βαλκιήλ, Ἀζαζήλ, Φαρμαρός, Ἀμαριήλ, Ἀναγημάς, Θαυσαήλ, Σαμιήλ, Σαρινάς, Ἐυμιήλ, Τυριήλ, Ἰουμιήλ, Σαριήλ.
verses.text_geez: ወእሎንቱ፡ አስማቲሆሙ፡ ለመላእክቲሆሙ፡ ሰማይዓዛ፡ ዘውእቱ፡ መልአኮሙ፡ አርቅባ፡ ራማኤል፡ ኮካባኤል፡ ታሚኤል፡ ራማኤል፡ ዳኒኤል፡ ሌቄል፡ ሳራቄል፡ አሳኤል፡ አርማርስ፡ በቶርኤል፡ አናኒኤል፡ ዘቄቤ፡ ሰምሳፔል፡ ሰትራኤል፡ ቱራኤል፡ ዮምያኤል፡ አራዜያል፡
verses.witness_primary: 4Q201 1 iii 5-10 + 4Q204 1 ii 24-29 (Milik 1976 pp. 150-156, 178-180) — CRITICAL: the 20 Watcher-chief names are preserved partially in Aramaic; the Aramaic onomastics is the most reliable witness to the original-language theonyms
verses.notes: **MAJOR LENS-RISK SITE — THE 20 WATCHER CHIEFS OF TENS.** The Aramaic onomastics are preserved (with some variation) in 4Q201 and 4Q204. **Etymology of the 20 names**: Šĕmīḥăzāh ('the Name has seen' or 'my name has seen'), ʾArʿătqōp (uncertain; possibly 'earth-power'), Rāmʾēl ('thunder of God' or 'morning/exaltation of God'), Kōkabʾēl ('star of God'), Bărāqʾēl ('lightning of God'), Zīqīʾēl ('shooting-star of God'), Ḥănānʾēl ('grace of God'), Šamšīʾēl ('sun of God'), Šaḥrīʾēl ('moon/dawn of God'), ʾAsʾēl (אסאל = ʿAsāʾēl, the same as Azazel — see ch 8), ʿAzazʾēl ('strength of God' OR 'azaz-El' the Azazel-figure of Lev 16). **The -ʾēl theophoric suffix** signals all 20 belong to the divine/angelic class; the prefixes encode their cosmic-domains (thunder, lightning, stars, sun, moon, weather, etc.) — these are the cosmic-knowledge specialists who later transmit their crafts to humanity (ch 8). Cross-corpus: cf. apkallū / Seven Sages tradition (Mesopotamian antediluvian-knowledge-transmitters); cf. Adapa myth; cf. Gilgamesh XI L308. The Watchers-as-apkallū parallel is one of the strongest cross-corpus links Reed 2005 + VanderKam 1984 develop. The Greek and Ge'ez name-lists corrupt many names (transliteration drift) — the Aramaic 4Q201/4Q204 readings are primary.

verses.text_greek: οὗτοι καὶ οἱ λοιποὶ πάντες ἐν τῷ ἑπτακοσιοστῷ ἔτει ἔλαβον ἑαυτοῖς γυναῖκας, καὶ ἤρξαντο μιαίνεσθαι ἐν αὐταῖς ἕως τοῦ κατακλυσμοῦ.
verses.translit: houtoi kai hoi loipoi pantes en tō heptakosiostō etei elabon heautois gynaikas, kai ērxanto miainesthai en autais heōs tou kataklysmou.
verses.text_geez: እሉ፡ እሙንቱ፡ መላእክተ፡ ዐሠርቱ፡ ወክልኤቱ፡ ወእሎንቱ፡ ካልኣን፡ ኵሎሙ፡ ምስሌሆሙ፡
verses.witness_primary: 4Q201 1 iii 11 (Milik 1976) — Aramaic preserves only the closing 'these are the chiefs of tens'
verses.notes: Closing formula: 'these are the chiefs of tens' — the 20 chiefs each command 10, for the total of 200 Watchers (cf. v. 6 'two hundred'). The Greek '700th year' (heptakosiostō etei) is a transmission corruption — Charles 1912 notes Ge'ez and the broader chronology suggest the Year of the World 1170. The Greek adds 'they began to defile themselves with them until the flood' — defines the temporal span of Watcher-human cohabitation.
